bibliography.note: Limnol. Oceanogr. 49(1): 69–75, 2004; authors Tom A. Sørnes and Dag L. Aksnes; title as cited

claims.claim: fish clear larvae at a visual planktivore's rate, Cmax = 3.42 × 10⁻⁷ L^2.94 m³/s, L in cm
claims.source_value: Cmax = 3.42 × 10⁻⁷ L^2.94 (r² = 0.92), Cmax in m³ s⁻¹, L in cm: the maximum clearance rate of visual planktivores (fish) on crustacean prey
claims.location: p. 74 (PDF p. 6), Discussion; abstract p. 69 (PDF p. 1); units in Fig. 1 caption p. 70 (PDF p. 2) and Eq. 3 p. 71–72
claims.conditions: log–log regression over n = 48 visual planktivores (adult and larval fish, 2–108 mm) from 22 published feeding studies plus the authors' own Gobiusculus flavescens (4 cm, 12 °C, Artemia nauplii); prey crustaceans 0.05–7.73 mm; only studies where feeding was not light-limited; L is the total or standard length as each study reported it; Cmax is the low-density (maximum) clearance rate, a in Holling's disc equation
claims.note: The formula, its units and its length scale are as cited. The source's prey are crustaceans (zooplankton, Artemia), not fish larvae: applying it to larvae is the project's step (the research note's §2 comparison with Pepin et al. 1992, Fuiman & Gamble 1988, Cowan & Houde 1993). The rewrite could say 'the maximum clearance rate of visual planktivores on crustacean zooplankton, in good light (Sørnes & Aksnes 2004)'.

claims.claim: the clearance scales ~L³ because the planktivore's search radius and speed both grow
claims.note: The exponent 2.94 (≈ L³) is confirmed, but the source's explanation is different: the exponent 'may reflect a three-dimensional search image of visual predators' (against 1.77, a two-dimensional sensory area, for tactile predators). It says nothing about search radius and swimming speed both growing; that mechanism is the research note's gloss. Reword the comment or cite a source for it.

tried.note: ASLO's old free back-issue URL is gone (the Wayback capture of it was used)

notes: Entry verdict 'corrected' only for the code comment's mechanism gloss (config.js:255); the paper's sentence in §4.5 is right. Other values in the source that may help: tactile (gelatinous) planktivores Cmax = 6.02 × 10⁻⁸ L^1.77 (r² 0.75); by dry mass, fish Cmax = 4.86 × 10⁻⁷ DW^0.95 (DW in mg, from DW = 5.62 × 10⁻⁴ L^3.09, Pepin 1995); G. flavescens's predation fell below 5–10 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ and stopped in darkness. The code's LARV_RHO 0.15 (the × 0.15 for zooplankton about) is not from this source.
